text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The turnout of the boring election day was 48 percent. Parliament Speaker Berri was the star.

-U.S. ambassador Jones visited President Hrawi. Washington to send invitations to members of the Lebanon consultative group this week. The committee was formed under an April ceasefire understanding which ended 17 days of Israeli bombardment of Lebanon.
-About 15,000 names had to be corrected on the voters' lists.
-Bank of Lebanon has become the biggest shareholder in Lebanon's national air carrier -- Middle East Airlines (MEA).

-The Lebanese Association for the Democracy of Elections reported incidents of voting in the name of dead people or emigrees, and police illegally entering many polling stations, some of which lacked isolating curtains for voting in secret.
-Citizens of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone voted for the first time on Sunday.
-Final results might not be issued before Tuesday.
